newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 to $15 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 to $15 lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $10 to $15 lower Tuesday on the heels of a weak performance in London overnight, traders said.
LIFFE cocoa futures were broadly lower early Tuesday, pressured by light fund selling. At the midday break, July was down 16 stg at 1,000 stg a tonne, with September 15 stg lower at 1,018.

Monday, New York cocoa futures ended lower in thin trade. July finished down $11 at $1,429 a tonne after trading from $1,428 to 1,445. September shed $10 to $1,457, while the remaining months ended $8 to $11 lower.
Technically, traders pegged July's near-term support at $1,412, followed by $1,404 to $1,400. A major downside objective was noted at $1,385.

To the upside, they said July cocoa would need to pierce the range of $1,450 to $1,460 to generate substantial new buying. Farther along, a chart gap formed in early April awaits at $1,480 to $1,501. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
